closest_prior_work.overlap: Heavy-ball momentum for stochastic gradient descent, with numerical experiments on artificial and real datasets; the same momentum mechanism of accumulating consistent gradient directions.
closest_prior_work.difference: Results are linear convergence rates under structured assumptions (consistent linear systems, projection-like Hessians), not accuracy after a fixed one-epoch budget on the repository's synthetic logistic-regression task with paired explore-split comparison against a reference SGD.

review_payload.delta_sentence: The candidate's contribution is a narrow, pre-specified empirical test of one bounded heavy-ball configuration against the repository's reference SGD on a synthetic logistic-regression task under a fixed one-epoch budget, which the cited paper (arXiv:1712.09677) does not perform; it should not be presented as a new momentum mechanism.

document.title: critical_review CAND-0001
document.summary: claude_code anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5: proceed

named_risks: Title claims faster convergence but the registered prediction is only final paired explore accuracy after one epoch; convergence speed is not measured.
Momentum coefficient and step size are not declared in the brief, so the configuration could be chosen after seeing results and conflicts with the no-grid-search rule.

Heavy-ball effectively scales the step by about 1/(1-beta); keeping LR 0.005 mixes a step-size change into the comparison, and the earlier LR 1.0 instability shows aggressive effective steps can diverge.
One epoch at 1,200 examples and batch 32 is about 38 updates, which may be too few for momentum to produce a 1.0 pp gain.
1.0 pp on 400 explore examples is four examples; with 3 paired seeds the variance may swamp the effect, and no variance or per-seed sign check is specified.
The statistical gate is referenced but not defined in min-setup or protocol.json beyond gate_comparison '>' and min_pairs 3.
Search and selection both use the explore split, so any post-hoc choice of configuration biases the result; only the c1 confirmation is independent.
The existing heavy-ball optimizer claim could not be verified because code/ lies outside the restricted working directory.
The reference config and execution path that the min-setup asks to be confirmed before freezing the harness are not evidenced.
review_payload.cheapest_discriminating_experiment: Pre-register one momentum config (e.g. beta=0.9 at reference LR 0.005) and the reference SGD; run both on seeds 42-44 against explore. Add a beta=0 run that must reproduce the reference exactly as a sanity check. Log per-step loss so the convergence-speed claim can be checked separately. Decide the gain using the paired mean in pp against the 1.0 pp threshold plus per-seed sign consistency; if the gain is below 1.0 pp or signs disagree, the idea fails at this budget.
missing_evidence: code/toytrain/methods.py showing the existing heavy-ball path and its correctness (not readable from the restricted working directory)
code/configs/reference.json confirming LR, batch, epochs and accumulation of the reference
The statistical test and guardrails that define a pass, in the protocol or a registered decision rule
A declared momentum coefficient and step size fixed before any run
SHA-256 check of cache/literature/1712.09677.pdf against the sha256 recorded in LIT-0001
Any variance estimate or prior run data showing that a 1.0 pp paired gain is distinguishable from seed noise on 400 explore examples

closest_prior_work.title: Why Warmup the Learning Rate? Underlying Mechanisms and Improvements
closest_prior_work.overlap: Studies linear learning-rate warmup from zero to a target rate for SGD and Adam, and argues that most warmup benefit comes from permitting a larger target rate (LIT-0002.v1.md, 核心方法).
closest_prior_work.difference: Does not study the project's pure-Python synthetic logistic regression, a one-epoch budget, or a fixed 10%-of-steps warmup held at the reference rate 0.005 (LIT-0002.v1.md, 实验设定与结果 and 最近邻差异). Its mechanism predicts little benefit when the target rate is not raised, so the candidate's likely outcome is a null result.

closest_prior_work.title: A Closer Look at Deep Learning Heuristics: Learning rate restarts, Warmup and Distillation
closest_prior_work.overlap: Treats learning-rate warmup as a stabilizing ingredient and analyzes how warmup limits early parameter changes (LIT-0003.v1.md, 核心方法).
closest_prior_work.difference: Studies deep networks (VGG-16 on CIFAR-10, 200 epochs, large or dynamic batches) rather than a shallow convex model on one epoch, and does not test a 10%-of-steps schedule at the reference rate (LIT-0003.v1.md, 实验设定与结果).

review_payload.delta_sentence: No cited paper tests a linear warmup over the first 10% of update steps, held at the reference SGD rate 0.005, on a one-epoch synthetic logistic-regression task with accuracy as the only metric; the delta is that configuration, which a reviewer can check against the setting rows of LIT-0002 and LIT-0003.

document.title: critical_review CAND-0002
document.summary: claude_code anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5: proceed

named_risks: Predicted outcome is a fail: warmup at a fixed 0.005 target lowers the average learning rate over only 38 updates, so accuracy is likely to fall or stay flat and miss the strict >1.0 pp gate (LIT-0002 lines 29-31; RV-0003).

Optimizer step interface receives only (params, grads, t) in code/toytrain/methods.py lines 11-19, and train.py line 112 supplies only the step index. A 10%-of-steps warmup needs a total-step value that is not available; passing it via config hardcodes 38, and train.py is outside the allowed edit scope.

The brief's 'more stable' claim is not measured: min-setup.v2.md line 30 operationalises the claim as final accuracy. A null result does not test stability, and a positive result would be read against the wrong target.

Resolution and noise: 400 explore examples give 0.25 pp per example, the gate is 4 examples, and 3 seed pairs of 38-update runs may vary by more than 1 pp. No reference seed spread has been measured yet.
Schedule underspecified: rounding of the 3.8-step warmup, whether the lr-0 first update counts as one of the 38 updates, and whether the ramp is t/warm or (t+1)/warm are not stated.
Weak novelty: 2406.09405 covers the same schedule family, and RV-0003 is a single reviewer's verdict, not an independent check. The value of the test is confirming a predicted null.
review_payload.cheapest_discriminating_experiment: Implement the warmup as a new class in methods.py with the total-step count passed through a config option, then run reference SGD (lr 0.005) and the warmup variant on seeds 42, 43, 44 against the explore split (6 runs, about 10 s each). Check that metrics.json reports steps=38 and that the first update uses lr 0. Compute the paired accuracy difference in pp. If the mean is at or below 1.0 pp, the candidate fails the gate and no confirmation run is warranted. If it is above, check whether it survives the seed spread before running c1.
missing_evidence: Reference SGD accuracy and seed-to-seed spread at 38 updates on the explore split, which sets the 1.0 pp threshold against real noise.
The exact warmup formula, step rounding, and how the total step count reaches the optimizer without editing train.py.
A decision on whether 'more stable' is dropped or restated as accuracy-only before any run.
LIT-0003.v1.md and the D-0021/D-0022 records, which were cited but not read in this review.
Whether the reference configuration is saturated or under-trained at 38 updates, which determines whether a warmup can help at all.

document.title: critical_review CAND-0002
document.summary: claude_code anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5: proceed

named_risks: Novelty review RV-0003 and both literature notes assess revision 1 (linear 10% warmup, sha dd291ec9), but the pool now holds revision 2 (sha 774e430b) describing cosine decay across the epoch; the prior-art assessment does not cover the current candidate.
Candidate title (linear warmup) and summary/mechanism (cosine decay) in candidates.json disagree; closest_work for revision 2 is generic.

The Alpha schedule (warmup length, peak rate, post-warmup behaviour) is not pre-registered in min-setup.v2.md or protocol.v1.json, which only pre-register Zebra; the configuration could be chosen after seeing explore results.
Alpha has no feasible or feasibility_reasons fields in candidates.json, so the discovery gate outcome for Alpha cannot be verified from the pool.

Expected effect is likely null: holding the reference rate 0.005 lowers average step size within one epoch, and LIT-0002 says warmup benefit may depend on raising the target rate; the 1.0 pp strict-gain bar on 400 examples with three paired seeds is unlikely to be cleared.
Explore is used both to compare Alpha and Zebra and as the search split, so choosing the better candidate there inflates the apparent gain; the single c1 confirmation is the only independent check.
The code/ files named in the brief (train.py, methods.py, run.py, reference.json) could not be read from the research directory, so the reference-path and harness claims are unverified.
review_payload.cheapest_discriminating_experiment: After pre-registering one explicit Alpha schedule (linear warmup over the first 10% of steps at rate 0.005, then hold) and recording it as a protocol artifact, run baseline and Alpha paired on the explore split for seeds 42, 43, 44 (about 10 s per run) and check whether the paired mean accuracy difference is strictly above 1.0 pp. Also run the same paired comparison for the cosine-decay revision 2 if it is kept, so the two revisions are not conflated. A paired mean at or below 1.0 pp supports the expected null and argues against spending the c1 confirmation.
missing_evidence: A discovery-gate output for CAND-0002 at revision 2 (the gate result the user asked for is not in the cited files).
A novelty review and literature check of the revision-2 cosine-decay method, or a recorded decision that revision 2 is withdrawn.
A pre-registered Alpha configuration (warmup steps, peak rate, schedule after warmup) in a protocol or setup file.
Literature records D-0021 and D-0022 and the cache/literature PDFs for the candidate's literature list.
Readable code/ sources (train.py, methods.py, run.py, configs/reference.json) to confirm the reference path and that an Alpha schedule can be expressed without changing evaluation code.
Feasibility assessment for Alpha, comparable to Zebra's feasible flag.
